name: Multi-Branch nftables + QoS Lab
summary: A fictional education and software company with a headquarters in Ankara, an Istanbul hub (VPN hub, DMZ, data center), a London office and an academic campus of 10,000 students. Each site has its own /16, role-based VLANs and a firewall HA pair managed from one FortiManager, with dual ISPs (SD-WAN failover; ULAKNET plus a commercial line at the campus). The website, mobile app API and LMS sit behind a Cloudflare WAF with ModSecurity at the origin. Administration is only through a role-based VPN with MFA and a bastion; there is no public SSH. Policy is default deny with a reason for every rule, and logs follow KVKK, Law 5651 and UK GDPR. A single Linux machine with nftables and tc HTB reproduces the rule logic as a tested lab (68 of 68 policy tests pass).

chosen.reason: 6 Gbps threat protection (datasheet) against a 500 Mbps link leaves headroom for IPS and SSL inspection plus growth; active-passive HA pair with session sync, managed from the central FortiManager. Price is per unit: list price of the hardware with 1-year FortiCare Premium and UTP bundle; an HA pair needs two units.

alternatives.reason: Not chosen: 20 Gbps is far more than a 500 Mbps headquarters needs and costs nearly three times as much per unit; revisit if the link grows past several Gbps.
Not chosen: 0.7 Gbps threat protection leaves only 40% headroom over the 500 Mbps link, while the headquarters also carries inter-site VPN and six VLANs.

Not chosen: about 1.0 Gbps threat prevention is enough today but leaves little growth, and a second vendor adds a separate management plane that FortiManager cannot manage. Price is approximate (about EUR 3,680 for hardware plus 1-year Threat Prevention, converted); verify with a quote.
Not chosen: free and capable, but no vendor support, no shared policy package with the other sites, and IPS tuning becomes our own job.

remoteAccess.note: No public SSH. Admins use a role-based VPN with MFA into a bastion in the Istanbul management VLAN; developers and staff get separate VPN pools that reach only their own segments. Every site builds its own IPsec tunnel to the Istanbul hub over both ISPs (SD-WAN failover).

monitoring.siem: Wazuh as the SIEM with FortiAnalyzer for firewall logs; FW-* log prefixes and tc counters in the lab. Log retention: hot 90 days in the SIEM, then a hashed read-only archive until the retention period ends (2 years for campus, guest and office access logs under Law 5651; 1 year for hosting and admin audit logs; UK GDPR logs 12 months unless a longer need is documented).
monitoring.owner: Campus SOC (2 analysts) owns security alerts; branch IT owns uptime and bandwidth. Every alert has a named owner and escalation goes through the SOC runbook.
monitoring.alertSink: Wazuh dashboard for triage; a Telegram channel only for high-severity blocks (VPN and management denies, WAF spikes), with outbound ALLOW and DNS noise filtered out.
monitoring.appVsSecurity: Application and bandwidth monitoring (uptime, tc and shaper counters, Prometheus/Grafana planned) goes to branch IT; security events (FW-* logs, WAF and ModSecurity blocks, VPN and management denies) go to the SOC in Wazuh. Operations also cover KVKK and UK GDPR privacy duties, nightly encrypted config backup stored at another site with a tested restore, and a monthly patch and firmware window with out-of-cycle patching for exploited vulnerabilities.

cveWatch.note: Authentication bypass in the FortiCloud SSO login, exploited in the wild. Temporary mitigation: FortiCloud SSO administrative login off, management interfaces reachable only from the management VLAN through the bastion, MFA for administrators. Permanent fix: upgrade to a fixed release (7.4.11 or 7.6.6 and later; check Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-060 for your branch) in the next out-of-cycle window, passive HA unit first, then review administrator accounts and rotate credentials.
